rationale: Three major patch findings: (CR-001) ?? operator passes through empty string — use || instead; (CR-002) type should be string | null to reflect possible API null; (CR-003) test suite missing null and empty-string cases. List-view inconsistency deferred as out-of-scope per ticket affected areas. AC-3 partially met: only one provider name exercised in tests. No security or breaking-change risk flags.

business_review.notes: provider_name is rendered directly when present; test confirms CodeAnalysisProvider is displayed.

business_review.criterion: Generic Provider no longer shown when actual name is available
business_review.notes: Fallback to humanize(indexType) only activates when provider_name is absent; test asserts queryByText('Provider') is null when name is set.

business_review.criterion: Consistent display for all supported provider types
business_review.notes: Runtime logic is generic (renders whatever API returns) but only one provider name is tested; list view inconsistency deferred as out-of-scope.

business_review.criterion: No regression for other data source types
business_review.notes: provider_name is optional; absent on non-provider types causing fallback to humanize(indexType) unchanged.

standards_review.notes: Display-only change; no auth, injection, or unsafe data handling.

findings.problem: The ?? operator passes through an empty string, so provider_name: '' renders a blank Data Source Type field instead of falling back to humanize(indexType).
findings.impact: A provider data source with a blank provider_name shows nothing in the sidebar type field.

findings.problem: provider_name is typed as string | undefined but the API may return null; downstream consumers trusting the TypeScript type will skip null guards.
findings.impact: Future code accessing provider_name without null guards may throw at runtime if the API sends null.
findings.recommendation: Widen the type declaration to provider_name?: string | null in DataSourceDetailsResponse.

findings.problem: The test suite has no cases for provider_name: null or provider_name: '' — the two runtime values most likely to cause a display regression.
findings.impact: A backend change returning null or empty string would silently break the display with no test catching it.
findings.recommendation: Add test cases for provider_name: null and provider_name: '' each asserting the humanized fallback is rendered.
